description: Defines how A.R.I.A. creates, represents, prioritizes, updates, suppresses, rules out, confirms, combines, and reactivates diagnostic hypotheses during microwave backhaul reasoning.

core_principle.statement: A hypothesis is a candidate explanation for one or more observed conditions. Hypotheses remain provisional until sufficient evidence supports confirmation and shall compete, coexist, weaken, strengthen, or be ruled out as evidence changes.
principles: Do not confuse plausibility with proof.
Do not confuse historical frequency with current diagnosis.
Do not discard alternatives merely because one hypothesis currently leads.
Do not preserve weak hypotheses indefinitely when evidence has materially ruled them out.
Allow multiple simultaneous failure modes when technically plausible.
Preserve an unknown explanation when the modeled hypothesis set may be incomplete.

hypothesis_statuses.name: CANDIDATE
hypothesis_statuses.description: Technically plausible hypothesis generated for evaluation.

hypothesis_statuses.name: ACTIVE
hypothesis_statuses.description: Hypothesis currently participating in diagnostic reasoning.

hypothesis_statuses.name: LEADING
hypothesis_statuses.description: Hypothesis currently having the strongest justified support among the applicable candidate explanations.

hypothesis_statuses.name: SUPPORTED
hypothesis_statuses.description: Evidence materially supports the hypothesis but confirmation requirements are not satisfied.

hypothesis_statuses.name: WEAKENED
hypothesis_statuses.description: Evidence has materially reduced support for the hypothesis.

hypothesis_statuses.name: DORMANT
hypothesis_statuses.description: Hypothesis remains technically possible but currently has insufficient probability or relevance to justify active diagnostic effort.

hypothesis_statuses.name: RULED_OUT
hypothesis_statuses.description: Available evidence is sufficient to remove the hypothesis from active consideration under the current technical state.

hypothesis_statuses.name: CONFIRMED
hypothesis_statuses.description: Available evidence satisfies applicable diagnostic confirmation requirements.

hypothesis_statuses.name: SUPERSEDED
hypothesis_statuses.description: A more precise or technically appropriate hypothesis has replaced this hypothesis while preserving its historical role.

hypothesis_statuses.name: MERGED
hypothesis_statuses.description: The hypothesis has been incorporated into another hypothesis because they represented the same underlying explanation.

generation_sources.name: KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH
generation_sources.description: Failure modes connected to observed symptoms, products, configurations, components, topologies, or technical mechanisms.

generation_sources.name: EXPERIENCE_LEDGER
generation_sources.description: Failure modes observed in sufficiently similar historical cases.

generation_sources.name: USER_HISTORY
generation_sources.description: Historically relevant failure patterns associated with the applicable user.

generation_sources.name: PRODUCT_HISTORY
generation_sources.description: Historically relevant failure patterns associated with the applicable product or variant.

generation_sources.name: MANUFACTURER_HISTORY
generation_sources.description: Historically relevant failure patterns associated with the applicable manufacturer.

generation_sources.name: CURRENT_EVIDENCE
generation_sources.description: Candidate explanations directly suggested by current measurements, alarms, configuration, visual evidence, logs, or test results.

generation_sources.name: TECHNICAL_INFERENCE
generation_sources.description: A technically valid explanation inferred from relationships between current observations.

generation_sources.name: UNKNOWN_BUCKET
generation_sources.description: Explicit representation of explanations not currently modeled or recognized.

generation_process.name: IDENTIFY_EXPLAINED_SYMPTOMS
generation_process.description: Determine which canonical symptoms require explanation.

generation_process.name: RETRIEVE_APPLICABLE_FAILURE_MODES
generation_process.description: Retrieve failure modes capable of producing the symptoms within the resolved technical context.

generation_process.name: RETRIEVE_HISTORICAL_FAILURES
generation_process.description: Retrieve relevant historical failure modes using contextual similarity.

generation_process.name: APPLY_TECHNICAL_CONSTRAINTS
generation_process.description: Remove technically impossible candidates while preserving uncertain candidates.

generation_process.name: DEDUPLICATE
generation_process.description: Merge semantically equivalent hypotheses referring to the same underlying technical condition.

generation_process.name: ADD_UNKNOWN
generation_process.description: Add unknown or unmodeled hypothesis mass when the candidate set cannot reasonably be assumed exhaustive.

generation_process.name: INITIALIZE_PRIORS
generation_process.description: Assign regularized starting probabilities before applying current evidence.

hierarchical_hypotheses.description: ARIA may begin with a broad hypothesis and progressively refine it into more specific hypotheses as evidence becomes available.
rules: Broad hypotheses may remain active while insufficient evidence exists to justify greater specificity.
A child hypothesis inherits technical compatibility constraints from its parent.
Confirmation of a specific child hypothesis may supersede broader parent hypotheses for diagnosis while preserving lineage.
Probability assigned to hierarchical hypotheses shall avoid double counting parent and child explanations.

evidence_effects.name: STRONGLY_SUPPORTS
evidence_effects.description: Evidence substantially increases support for the hypothesis.

evidence_effects.name: SUPPORTS
evidence_effects.description: Evidence moderately increases support for the hypothesis.

evidence_effects.name: WEAKLY_SUPPORTS
evidence_effects.description: Evidence slightly increases support for the hypothesis.

evidence_effects.name: NEUTRAL
evidence_effects.description: Evidence has no material effect on the hypothesis.

evidence_effects.name: WEAKENS
evidence_effects.description: Evidence moderately reduces support for the hypothesis.

evidence_effects.name: STRONGLY_WEAKENS
evidence_effects.description: Evidence substantially reduces support for the hypothesis.

evidence_effects.name: CONTRADICTS
evidence_effects.description: Evidence is materially inconsistent with the hypothesis.

evidence_effects.name: EXCLUDES
evidence_effects.description: Validated evidence establishes a condition incompatible with the hypothesis under the applicable technical model.

required_questions: Is this evidence technically relevant to the hypothesis?
Is the evidence applicable to the current product and context?
Is the evidence current enough to represent the present condition?
Is the evidence independent from other supporting evidence?
Does the evidence support or contradict the mechanism predicted by the hypothesis?
How strongly should the evidence change belief?

rules: Specific historical populations may influence priors more strongly when sufficient sample size and contextual similarity exist.
Broad populations shall remain available as fallback priors when specific historical populations are sparse.
Small sample populations shall be regularized toward broader applicable populations.
Historical priors shall not override strong current evidence.
Historical priors shall preserve their source population and sample size.

regularization.purpose: Prevent ARIA from overlearning from small or noisy historical samples.
rules: One successful case shall not establish a dominant future prior.
Small user-specific samples shall be blended with broader applicable experience.
As validated sample size increases, specific historical populations may receive greater influence.
Cases with restricted learning confidence shall contribute proportionally less weight.
Cases excluded from learning shall contribute no learned probability weight.
ARIA shall maintain multiple active hypotheses when technically justified.
A leading hypothesis shall not cause automatic suppression of viable alternatives.
Diagnostic actions should preferentially discriminate between high-value competing hypotheses.
Probability shall be redistributed only according to the applicable probability model.
Evidence supporting one hypothesis does not automatically weaken another unless the hypotheses compete or the evidence has discriminatory value.

coexisting_hypotheses.description: ARIA shall support cases where multiple failures exist simultaneously.
rules: Potentially coexisting hypotheses shall not be forced into a mutually exclusive probability distribution.
ARIA may create hypothesis groups representing independent or partially dependent fault domains.
Resolution of one failure shall not automatically close the case when unresolved symptoms remain.
Remaining symptoms shall be reevaluated after each confirmed correction.

hypothesis_relationships.name: MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE
hypothesis_relationships.description: Both hypotheses cannot simultaneously explain the defined condition under the applicable technical model.

hypothesis_relationships.name: CAN_COEXIST
hypothesis_relationships.description: Both hypotheses may simultaneously be true.

hypothesis_relationships.name: DEPENDENT
hypothesis_relationships.description: Probability or validity of one hypothesis depends materially on another.

hypothesis_relationships.name: CAUSAL_CHAIN
hypothesis_relationships.description: One hypothesis may cause or contribute to the other.

hypothesis_relationships.name: SHARED_PARENT
hypothesis_relationships.description: Hypotheses are more specific alternatives beneath a common broader hypothesis.

hypothesis_relationships.name: OVERLAPPING
hypothesis_relationships.description: Hypotheses partially describe the same technical mechanism and require careful probability handling to avoid double counting.

hypothesis_relationships.name: UNRELATED
hypothesis_relationships.description: No material dependency is currently known.

requirements: Evidence materially incompatible with the hypothesis exists.
Evidence quality is sufficient for the technical consequence of ruling out the hypothesis.
Applicability of the excluding evidence is established.
Material contradictions in the excluding evidence have been addressed.
rules: Low probability alone shall not rule out a hypothesis.
Failure to find supporting evidence shall not automatically rule out a hypothesis.
A hypothesis may be ruled out when validated evidence establishes an incompatible condition.
Rule-out reason and supporting evidence shall be preserved.

reactivation_policy.description: A ruled-out or dormant hypothesis may return to active reasoning only when the technical state materially changes.
rules: Reactivation requires an explicit reason.
ARIA shall preserve why the hypothesis was previously ruled out.
Reactivation shall not erase prior probability history.
Repeated unjustified reactivation shall be treated as a reasoning-loop defect.
No universal probability threshold alone shall confirm every diagnosis.
Higher-risk corrective actions may require stronger confirmation.
Direct isolation evidence may justify confirmation more strongly than historical frequency.
Material unexplained contradictions shall reduce confirmation confidence.
ARIA may maintain a provisional diagnosis when confirmation requirements are not satisfied.

unknown_hypothesis.purpose: Prevent ARIA from forcing every case into an existing failure mode.
rules: Unknown may receive nonzero probability whenever the candidate hypothesis set is not known to be exhaustive.
Unknown probability may increase when known hypotheses are weakened without another explanation gaining support.
Unknown probability should decrease when evidence strongly supports sufficiently comprehensive modeled explanations.
A persistent high unknown probability should trigger broader knowledge retrieval, alternative hypothesis generation, or escalation.

hypothesis_pruning.purpose: Control computational growth without destroying diagnostically meaningful alternatives.
rules: Pruning shall not delete hypothesis history.
Low-probability hypotheses with high consequence or inexpensive discriminating tests may remain active.
Dormant hypotheses remain retrievable.
The number of actively scored hypotheses may be bounded independently from the number of hypotheses preserved in case history.

active_set_policy.description: ARIA shall maintain a manageable working set of hypotheses while preserving the broader hypothesis graph.
rules: These values are computational defaults rather than technical limits.
ARIA may exceed the soft maximum when case complexity justifies it.
Hypotheses outside the active set remain available as dormant candidates.
High-consequence hypotheses may remain active despite relatively low probability.

semantic_rules.rule: A hypothesis is a temporary explanatory model and shall never be treated as fact merely because ARIA generated it.
ARIA shall preserve meaningful competing explanations until evidence justifies weakening, dormancy, rule-out, merging, supersession, or confirmation.
The leading hypothesis is the currently strongest candidate, not necessarily the diagnosis.
Historical experience influences prior probability but current evidence determines whether the historical expectation remains applicable.
ARIA shall not repeatedly resurrect a ruled-out hypothesis without new technical justification.
Hypothesis probability changes shall preserve traceability to the evidence and operations responsible for the change.
ARIA shall distinguish broad fault domains from specific root causes and progressively refine hypotheses when evidence supports greater specificity.
Parent and child hypotheses shall not be independently counted as separate competing causes when they represent the same causal explanation at different levels of specificity.
Multiple simultaneous faults are valid and shall not be forced into a single-root-cause model.
Unknown is preferable to an unsupported known hypothesis.
Hypothesis pruning is a computational optimization and shall not destroy diagnostic history.
ARIA shall avoid confirmation bias by selecting diagnostic actions according to discriminatory utility rather than merely seeking evidence supporting the leading hypothesis.
Evidence shall be allowed to increase the probability of an initially unlikely hypothesis when the evidence strongly discriminates in its favor.
ARIA shall distinguish correlation, mechanism compatibility, isolation evidence, and causal confirmation.
When all known hypotheses become weak, ARIA shall broaden the search space rather than artificially promoting the least-wrong known explanation.
